works.title: DBAASP V4: condition-resolved bioactivity and chemical structures for data-driven peptide and peptidomimetic discovery
works.abstract: The current peptide renaissance-driven by metagenomic and proteomic mining, molecular de-extinction, protein language models, and generative or evolutionary design-is producing millions of candidates, but useful machine learning depends on experimentally anchored, context-rich labels. The Database of Antimicrobial Activity and Structure of Peptides (DBAASP) is a manually curated resource linking peptides and peptidomimetics to quantitative antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer, hemolytic, and mammalian-cell cytotoxicity measurements and their experimental conditions. DBAASP v4 contains >25 000 entries and extends the resource from a sequence-centered database to a structure-aware repository. Major additions include systematic SMILES representations, enhanced annotation of intrachain bonds and ring architectures, dedicated antibiofilm, and synergy records, PubChem links, >9200 molecular-dynamics trajectories, and new prediction services. The condition-resolved data support supervised learning, strain-, and target-specific models, model calibration, and surrogate fitness functions for genetic algorithms. SMILES representations further enable modeling of noncanonical peptides and peptidomimetics that cannot be adequately described by sequence alone. DBAASP therefore complements large peptide catalogues by providing the experimentally curated activity and structure layers, needed to convert sequence information into testable predictions, design, and optimization of biologically active compounds. DBAASP v4 is freely available at https://dbaasp.org.

works.title: MultiTargetDB: a comprehensive database of multitarget ligands for polypharmacology research and drug discovery
works.abstract: Multitarget drug discovery has gained considerable traction in recent years, particularly for the treatment of complex diseases. Despite the growing demand for dedicated, well-curated resources to advance polypharmacology research and rational multitarget drug discovery, such resources remain severely limited. Here, we present MultiTargetDB, a database of multitarget ligands integrated with comprehensive biological annotations and measurement-level provenance. At the small molecule level, MultiTargetDB integrates chemical structures (including molecular scaffolds), their drug development stages, and target information, whereas at the target level, MultiTargetDB incorporates protein domains and families, functional associations, and pathway-disease annotations. The current release contains 173 977 multitarget molecules, 6496 protein targets, and 474 749 standardized quantitative bioactivity records, complemented by 46 234 high-confidence protein functional associations, 370 pathways from the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), and 2493 diseases. MultiTargetDB supports multitarget ligand retrieval, target-combination analysis, quantitative activity profiling, inspection of source-level evidence, and biological interpretation of molecule-target-pathway-disease relationships, with a natural-language query assistant facilitating flexible database exploration. The integrated quantitative, pharmacological and biological data further provide a basis for drug-repurposing exploration, computational modeling, and machine-learning applications. MultiTargetDB v1.0 is freely accessible at https://multitargetdb.inflygent.com/.

works.title: AnnelidaDB: a comprehensive platform of taxonomic and multi-omic resources across annelids
works.abstract: Annelids inhabit marine, freshwater, and terrestrial ecosystems and are important models for studying animal evolution, regeneration, and host-microbe interactions, yet their rapidly growing omics resources remain dispersed across repositories and publications. We developed AnnelidaDB (www.annelidadb.com), a species-centred database built on an updated phylogenetic framework that integrates genomes, mitochondrial genomes, transcriptomes, proteomes, epigenomes, single-cell datasets, host-associated symbiont genomes, and comparative synteny for Annelida. The current release covers 1121 species, including 152 species with nuclear genomes, 177 with mitochondrial genomes, 591 with transcriptome data, 5 with single-cell datasets comprising 209 802 cells, and 30 bacterial symbiont genomes. AnnelidaDB organizes these resources through 10 navigation directories and connects species, genome, gene, functional annotation, and gene-family records. Users can browse genomic assemblies, explore interactive single-cell atlases and 12 200 precomputed Oxford plots, run BLAST queries and search genes against the annelid-specific database, and submit chromosome-level data for syntenic analysis against 20 Annelida linkage groups. Sequences, annotations, and private results are available for download. As a comprehensive multi-omics resource dedicated to annelids, AnnelidaDB provides an accessible platform for comparative investigations of annelid genome evolution, adaptation, regeneration, and symbiosis.

works.title: PROTAC-DB 4.0: an expanded knowledgebase of targeted protein degradation modalities with AI-powered knowledge discovery
works.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) represent an emerging therapeutic modality that harnesses the ubiquitin-proteasome system to induce targeted protein degradation (TPD). Their event-driven and catalytic mechanisms provide new opportunities to target previously undruggable proteins. However, the rapid expansion of TPD technologies, including molecular glues (MGs) and X-functional targeting chimeras (XTACs), together with the increasing application of artificial intelligence (AI) in degrader design, highlights the need for comprehensive and continuously updated data resources. Here, we present PROTAC-DB 4.0, an expanded knowledgebase covering major targeted degradation and induced-proximity technologies. Compared with the previous version, PROTAC-DB 4.0 contains 15 502 PROTAC entries, together with 24 798 MG entries and 272 XTAC entries, with expanded experimental annotations, patent-derived compounds, and modality-specific data fields. A major advancement in PROTAC-DB 4.0 is the integration of a large language model and retrieval-augmented generation-based natural language query system, which connects structured database records with scientific literature to enable intuitive knowledge discovery across PROTACs, MGs, and XTACs. By combining comprehensive data curation with AI-assisted information retrieval, PROTAC-DB 4.0 provides an accessible platform to support degrader discovery, data-driven modeling, and rational design of next-generation targeted degradation and induced-proximity therapeutics. PROTAC-DB 4.0 is freely accessible at http://cadd.zju.edu.cn/protacdb/.

works.title: CAnDi: a global catalogue of anaerobic digestion microbiomes
works.abstract: Methanogenic environments harbour complex prokaryotic consortia that drive the anaerobic conversion of organic matter into methane and carbon dioxide. Beyond being key to the global carbon cycle, such processes have been steered into powerful biotechnologies for energy production in bioreactors. Decoding the functional and taxonomic landscape of these communities requires comprehensive surveys, including bacteriophages and plasmids, which, however, remain vastly underrepresented in current databases. Here, we present the microbial Catalogue of Anaerobic Digestion (CAnDi), a database comprising 36 480 prokaryotic genomes spanning 11 149 species recovered from 1256 metagenomic samples collected across bioreactors worldwide. The reconstructed metagenomes also encode ∼1.9 million viral and over 130 000 plasmid sequences. Identity clustering revealed ∼536 000 candidate viral species, of which 85% are novel relative to existing databases, as well as over 15 000 unique plasmids. Clusters of viral and plasmid proteins were generated de novo, totalling 1 721 182 and 123 813 distinct protein families, respectively. Together, these resources substantially advance previous systematic approaches to characterize anaerobic digestion microbiomes, providing an expanded foundation for investigating the ecological and evolutionary roles of the virome and plasmidome in methane-producing ecosystems. CAnDi is accessible via https://www.candi-db.org/.

works.title: LoGIC: a cross-species local gene-cluster integrative catalog
works.abstract: Homologous genes, especially those sharing close genomic locations and forming gene clusters, often have compensatory roles, therefore pose remarkable challenges for deciphering the functions and relationships of these genes. A comprehensive database of local homologous gene clusters with multimodal information would greatly facilitate such research. Here, we present LoGIC (https://omicslab.genetics.ac.cn/LoGIC/), a Local Gene-cluster Integrative Catalog that includes 20 306 local gene clusters identified from 30 representative eukaryotic species. In addition to the basic genomic features of each gene cluster, LoGIC also allows users to examine the sequence similarity of gene members within a cluster, the functional preference of clustered genes within a species, and the cross-species conservation of gene clusters. Information of tissue-wide expression profile and relationship with chromatin Hi-C structure is also available for human gene clusters. Together, LoGIC can facilitate studies of tandem gene duplication, paralog functional divergence, lineage-specific gene-family expansion, and evolutionary conservation or remodelling of homologous gene clusters across-species.

works.title: EVLncRNAs 4.0: an updated database of experimentally validated functional long non-coding RNAs with evidence-grounded AI access
works.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have diverse biological functions, but experimentally validated evidence remains scattered across the literature and is often context dependent. EVLncRNAs 4.0 (https://www.sdklab-biophysics-dzu.net/EVLncRNAs4/) updates our manually curated database of functional lncRNAs supported by low-throughput experiments. For this release, 16 581 publications indexed between 15 May 2023 and 15 May 2026 were retrieved and manually screened. Compared with EVLncRNAs 3.0, EVLncRNAs 4.0 contains 7808 functional lncRNAs (+26%) from 199 species (+23%), 2313 diseases (+34%), 28 757 curated functional records (+21%), and 18 380 molecular interactions (+25%). EVLncRNAs 4.0 also introduces two AI-assisted functions built on the curated evidence base. AI Search uses an enhanced retrieval-augmented generation framework with adaptive selection across Quick, Expanded, and Exhaustive retrieval modes and generates answers from retrieved EVLncRNAs records with PMID-linked citations. Benchmark evaluation showed complete request execution, high retrieval coverage and full citation validity within the supplied evidence context. Functional Overview retrieves and aggregates lncRNA- and species-specific curated records before generating concise evidence-based summaries. In both functions, language models synthesize retrieved evidence rather than serve as independent sources of biological knowledge. EVLncRNAs 4.0 therefore provides an expanded, experimentally grounded resource for accessing and interpreting functional lncRNA evidence across species and biological contexts.

works.title: MetabDB: an integrated resource for human metabolic measures, disease associations, and genetic evidence
works.abstract: Population-scale metabolomics studies have linked metabolic measures to diseases, quantitative traits, and genetic variation, but the results are scattered across assay platforms, phenotype definitions, and analytical formats. MetabDB integrates 16 public studies spanning nuclear magnetic resonance, mass spectrometry, and lipidomics. The current release contains 2663 metabolic measures, 3524 diseases and outcomes, 3382 other genome-wide association traits, and 2025 molecular quantitative trait locus (QTL) targets. MetabDB links genomic variants, genes and proteins, metabolic measures, and diseases or traits through variant/QTL associations, fine-mapping, rare-variant or burden analyses, colocalization, Mendelian randomization, and population associations. Metabolic measures areretained in their source-reported forms, including compounds, lipid species, lipoprotein measures, ratios, percentages, and derived traits. Gene- and protein-level evidence can be examined alongside genomic signals and related disease or trait evidence for the same metabolic measure. Source information and reported analytical details are retained, including the source study, original variable or phenotype definition, assay, unit, exposure scale, analytical model, and statistics where available. Search, browse, and colocalization pages, together with gene evidence breadth and disease-association profiles, provide access to these records. MetabDB is freely available at http://www.mulinlab.org/metabdb/.

works.title: PathoEvo: an interactive single-cell database for exploring disease progression and pathological evolution
works.abstract: Disease progression is driven by coordinated changes in tissue microenvironments, cellular composition, cell states, and transcriptional programmes. Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing enable these changes to be studied at cellular resolution. However, public disease-associated datasets are often organized within individual studies and annotated using heterogeneous clinical, pathological, or molecular staging systems, limiting comparison across disease stages and datasets. Here, we present PathoEvo (https://biomedlab-ai.com/pathoevo/), a disease-associated single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic database centred on disease progression. PathoEvo integrates 7 452 971 cells or nuclei from 981 samples and 59 datasets, covering 18 diseases and 27 progression frameworks. Through manual curation, unified processing, metadata harmonization, cell-type annotation, and stage mapping, PathoEvo organizes heterogeneous datasets into standardized resources organized around disease progression. Its data and analytical functions span three complementary levels, allowing users to examine changes in cellular composition associated with disease stage and cell states, characterize sample-level molecular variation across disease progression, and investigate gene expression dynamics across relevant cell populations and samples. Structured search and browsing further facilitate dataset discovery and navigation of stage-resolved information across diseases and staging systems. PathoEvo provides an integrative resource for investigating pathological evolution and comparing cellular and molecular patterns of disease progression across datasets at single-cell resolution.

works.title: More than just a centromere: evolution of a structural supergene causing female meiotic drive in monkeyflowers
works.abstract: Abstract Meiotic drivers capitalize on vulnerabilities in eukaryotic meiosis and gametogenesis to gain greater-than-equal transmission to the next generation. In most plants and animals, asymmetric female meiosis presents an arena for meiotic drive, as centromeric variants may bias their segregation to the one egg cell. Although centromeric drive is predicted to be pervasive, its mechanisms and consequences remain obscure. Here, we build on representative chromosome-scale assemblies of yellow monkeyflowers (Mimulus guttatus species complex) to compare three functionally distinct haplotypes at Meiotic Drive Locus on Chromosome 11 (MDL11). The driving D allele at MDL11 was previously shown to be centromere-containing, costly, and maintained as a balanced polymorphism in wild M. guttatus populations. D has diverged from nondrivers via at least two major rearrangements (including a hemicentric inversion creating linked arrays of centromeric satellite Cent728 separated by > 200 trapped genes), massive expansions of a novel MDL11-specific subfamily of satellite repeats (Cent728D) that increase the length of the driver chromosome by >50% over homologues, and the build-up of a 2Mb D-exclusive pericentromeric region containing ∼37 extra D-associated genes duplicated and translocated from diverse genomic sources. Differences in centromeric satellite arrays, particularly the recent expansion of Cent728D are primary candidates for generating female meiotic drive. However, substantial divergence in gene content and sequence among the three haplotypes also points to candidate genic modifiers that may enhance D drive and contribute to differences in drive-susceptibility among non-drivers. Overall, our findings support the sequential buildup of this model centromeric driver, reveal intriguing parallels with other selfish supergenes, and provide a strong platform for understanding the mechanisms of its dramatic violation of Mendelian rules.

works.title: Biallelic germline variants in the hematologic malignancy predisposition gene DDX41 cause retinal dystrophy through dysregulation of retinal homeostasis
works.abstract: DDX41 encodes a DEAD-box ATPase RNA helicase essential for RNA splicing, innate immune signaling, and hematopoiesis. Monoallelic germline DDX41 pathogenic variants represent the most common inherited predisposition to adult-onset myeloid malignancies, but their role in retinal disorders has remained unexplored. Using next-generation sequencing, we identified nine distinct germline DDX41 variants in biallelic combinations across ten families with inherited retinal disease, including one family previously reported by Diness et al. (2018), in whom retinal involvement had not been recognized. Patient fibroblasts homozygous for the missense variant c.1187T > C (p.I396T) and Ddx41 I396T/I396T mouse retinas exhibited markedly reduced DDX41 protein levels. Electroretinography demonstrated early and severe visual dysfunction, establishing a direct requirement for DDX41 in retinal physiology. DDX41 is localized to nuclei of all major retinal cell types and to photoreceptor synapses. Biochemical assays showed that disease-associated variants disrupted RNA binding through misfolding and aggregation, causing loss of function. Transcriptomic and proteomic profiling of mutant retinas revealed dysregulation of pathways involved in photoreceptor maintenance, RNA processing, immune signaling, and adherens junctions. Immunofluorescence analysis demonstrated altered Müller glial organization, and reactive gliosis. Retinal interactome analysis further characterized DDX41-associated protein networks enriched in synaptic function, RNA processing, and membrane trafficking pathways. These findings identify DDX41 deficiency as a previously unrecognized cause of early-onset severe retinal dystrophy (EOSRD). Clinically, they extend the spectrum of DDX41‑related disease beyond hematologic malignancies, indicating that individuals with biallelic variants may present with early‑onset visual impairment. More broadly, this work underscores the essential role of RNA helicases in neural tissue integrity and shows that disruption of DDX41 impairs retinal homeostasis and visual function.

works.title: A haplotype reference panel constructed from 490,319 UK Biobank genomes improves genotype imputation for global populations
works.abstract: Abstract Here we constructed a genotype imputation reference panel from whole-genome sequencing data from 490,319 UK Biobank (UKB) participants 1 and enabled both standalone and cloud-based phasing and imputation through EagleImp 2 and EagleImp-RAP within the UK Biobank Research Analysis Platform. The UKB reference panel achieves lower phasing switch error rates than the widely used TOPMed r3 panel (133,597 individuals) for all global superpopulations except AMR and for 25 of 26 1000 Genomes Project subpopulations. Imputation accuracy, measured by MAE, improved for 4 of 5 superpopulations and 12 subpopulations for variants with minor allele frequencies down to 0.01%. Estimated squared correlation further improved across all 5 superpopulations and 22 subpopulations, with the largest gains in East and South Asian populations. Reimputation of COVID-19 genome-wide association study datasets from Italy, Germany, Spain and Norway 3,4 demonstrated that common-variant imputation remains unsaturated, enhancing the discovery of genome-wide significant loci and improving fine-mapping resolution.

works.title: Ethical challenges in patient-focused drug development for rare genetic diseases
Mechanisms and regulation of proteolytic DNA–protein crosslink repair
CellPatch: a flexible and efficient framework for single-cell foundation models empowered by heuristic gene patching
works.abstract: Abstract Foundation models have advanced single-cell omics analysis but often remain too complex for practical use. We present CellPatch, a lightweight foundation model combining cross-attention with heuristic gene patching to reduce computational complexity during pretraining and fine-tuning while enabling inspection of gene-attention patterns. Across single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets spanning multiple organs and tissue states, CellPatch achieves state-of-the-art performance on diverse prediction tasks. Its modular design supports linear, adapter-based and task-specific architectures, enabling CellPatch to be adapted to diverse biological tasks.

works.title: dictyBase 2026: a reimplementation of the Dictyostelium model organism database on minimal infrastructure
works.abstract: Dictyostelium discoideum is a model organism used to investigate a wide array of biological processes including chemotaxis, cell motility, phagocytosis, multicellular development, and autophagy. Many of its genes have human orthologs implicated in disease, making it a useful model organism for studying conditions ranging from cancer to neurodegeneration. dictyBase has served this community for two decades as a home for genomic data, protocols, a stock center, and community news. Here we describe a complete reimplementation of dictyBase as a self-contained service that uses static data files rather than a database server. Each gene record gathers curated function, human-disease context, developmental expression, and protein structure in a single webpage. The site also provides tools for sequence search, genome browsing, enrichment analysis, and experimental design. The complete Dicty Stock Center catalog of 7055 strains and 1265 plasmids is included, and both can be ordered from the site. New literature is curated by an author-in-the-loop pipeline. A language model drafts the annotations, the authors of the paper correct them, and a curator approves them. Analyses can be run on curator-approved annotations alone or extended to include those still awaiting review. dictyBase is freely available at https://dicty.org.

works.title: ARIEL: an openly accessible database of experimental RNA–ligand binding affinities paired with 3D structures
works.abstract: RNA is an increasingly attractive target for small-molecule therapeutics, yet the rational design and computational modelling of RNA-binding small molecules are constrained by the scarcity of experimentally measured binding affinities linked to 3D structures. Here we present ARIEL (Affinity Resource for Interactions of RNA and Ligands), an openly accessible, manually curated database that pairs experimentally determined dissociation constants (Kd) of RNA-ligand complexes with the corresponding experimental structures. We screened 6954 RNA-containing structures from the Protein Data Bank, extracted 2843 complexes with a small ligand, and manually curated the associated primary literature to retrieve the corresponding Kd values. This yielded a nonredundant dataset of 278 RNA-ligand complexes with experimental affinities, including 179 unique ligands bound to 171 different RNA targets, with Kd values spanning nine orders of magnitude (-log Kd 2.1-11.0). Each entry also provides the Kd measurement method and conditions, full literature provenance, ligand physicochemical descriptors, and binding-pocket annotations, with direct cross-links between structures, ligands and source publications. ARIEL will be maintained through regular, versioned releases; it is freely available at https://aocdweb.com/BioTools/ARIEL/.

works.title: XYcellAtlas: a cell-type- and spatial-resolved pan-cancer atlas of sex-biased and Y chromosome loss-associated molecular signatures
works.abstract: Sex is a critical determinant of cancer susceptibility, clinical prognosis, and therapeutic response. Sex chromosome aberrations, particularly somatic loss of the Y chromosome (LOY) in male malignancies, exert profound impacts on transcriptional regulation, tumor immune microenvironment remodeling, and malignant progression, highlighting an urgent demand for comprehensive integration of single-cell and spatial omics profiles dissecting sex-biased and LOY landscapes across human cancers. Here, we developed XYcellAtlas (http://www.xycellatlas.top/), an integrative database for integration and multidimensional visualization of sex disparities and LOY features across human tissues at single-cell transcriptomic, epigenomic, and spatial-transcriptomic resolutions. This resource aggregates data from 6764 patient samples covering 18 cancer types, eight precancerous lesions, and 21 tissue origins, encompassing over 25.8 million single cells and one million spatial-transcriptomic spots. Leveraging random forest classifiers trained on normal tissue datasets, XYcellAtlas quantifies cell-type-specific LOY frequencies across cell types. Furthermore, it systematically catalogs sex-biased and LOY-associated molecular alterations, including differentially expressed genes, chromatin peaks, core transcription factors, as well as their functional annotations and dysregulatory signatures within malignant cells and the tumor microenvironment. In summary, XYcellAtlas provides a unified, all-in-one analytical platform enabling researchers to query, inspect, quantify, and visualize sex-associated and LOY-derived multi-omics features underlying tumor evolutionary processes.

works.title: STRAND: a comprehensive subcellular-resolved spatial transcriptome RNA architecture and navigation database
works.abstract: Subcellular RNA localization serves as a critical regulatory layer governing cellular polarization, local translation, and functional compartmentalization. Recent advances in high-resolution spatial transcriptomics have provided unprecedented opportunities to resolve these intracellular architectures at single-molecule resolution. However, relevant datasets are dispersed across studies and repositories, vary substantially in processing procedures and standards, severely limiting their cross-study reuse. To bridge this gap, we present STRAND (Subcellular-Resolved Spatial Transcriptome RNA Architecture and Navigation Database), a curated data resource and analysis platform for the automated harvesting, quality control, and interpretation of subcellular spatial transcriptomics data. Through an agent-assisted curation pipeline, STRAND has assembled 35 subcellular-resolution datasets from six major platforms, covering 17 tissue types in human and mouse and totalling ∼4.9 billion transcript coordinates. Building upon this standardized data resource, STRAND provides an analytical workflow spanning cell segmentation evaluation, cell-type annotation, RNA localization/colocalization pattern annotation, and subcellular compartment inference. Two case studies demonstrate that STRAND successfully identifies established RNA localization patterns in cultured cell lines and detects drug-induced RNA relocalization in cardiomyocytes. STRAND is openly available at https://strand.phasep.pro.

works.title: DiseaseCIO: a multi-omics atlas for characterizing clinical intervention outcomes across diverse diseases
works.abstract: Heterogeneity in clinical intervention outcomes across patients is a major barrier to precision medicine. The integration of multidimensional high-throughput omics can help reveal the molecular basis of differences in clinical interventions and provide insights into outcome prediction, prognostic stratification, regulatory patterns, and resistance mechanisms. We present DiseaseCIO (Disease Clinical Intervention Outcomes, http://db.edbc.org/DiseaseCIO/), a database that integrates microbiome, transcriptome, and epigenome data with human disease intervention outcomes. It is designed to characterize the molecular landscape associated with disease intervention outcomes at the individual patient level. DiseaseCIO encompasses 42 798 pretreatment samples from 94 disease states, covering 510 treatment regimens involving 377 pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions. These samples comprise four types of specimens collected from eight sampling locations. Using the customized iMOD workflow for multi-omics data processing, we generated 20 categories of molecular features and identified >1.84 million candidate feature-outcome associations. DiseaseCIO also provides interactive tools for differential analysis, prognostic evaluation, cross-omics correlation analysis, and cross-cohort integrative analysis of multidimensional features as well as enrichment analysis and signature construction for user-submitted feature sets. DiseaseCIO provides a molecular-level resource for exploring intervention outcome heterogeneity across diseases and identifying candidate multi-omics biomarkers associated with treatment response and prognosis.

works.title: ATAD2B governs epigenetic silencing of the epithelial program to fuel cancer metastasis and neuronal migration
works.abstract: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a pivotal developmental program that is frequently co-opted to drive cancer aggressiveness and metastasis. While the dynamic remodelling of histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac) landscapes is a hallmark of EMT, the specific chromatin readers decoding these epigenetic signals remain largely unknown. Here, we identify ATAD2B as a novel H3K27ac reader essential for cell migration in both cancer metastasis and brain development. Multi-omics profiling revealed that, at EMT onset, ATAD2B targets H3K27ac at active epithelial identity genes via its bromodomain and recruits HDAC1 to epigenetically silence them, enforcing a mesenchymal state. ATAD2B loss impairs migration and invasion in breast cancer lines and Patient-Derived organoids, whereas its overexpression accelerates in vivo lung metastasis and correlates with poor patient survival. Furthermore, ATAD2B promotes the migration of newborn neurons in the developing brain. Our findings establish ATAD2B as a versatile chromatin reader orchestrating cell motility across development and disease.

works.title: kri-1/KRIT1 promotes innate immune and lipid homeostasis in the C. elegans intestine
works.abstract: Animals must differentially allocate essential metabolic resources in response to changing environmental conditions to ensure reproductive success. For example, adult C. elegans coordinate innate immune defenses during infection and also allocate fat stores to the germline, each of which are required for evolutionary fitness. The genetic mechanisms that integrate resource allocation and host defenses in this context, however, are not fully understood. From a forward genetic screen for novel regulators of innate immune gene transcription, we identified kri-1, the nematode homolog of human Krev interaction trapped protein KRIT1. Mutations in human KRIT1 underlie cerebral cavernous malformations, a disease marked by defects in vascular integrity. Similarly, C. elegans kri-1/KRIT1 is required for the integrity of the intestinal epithelial cell barrier. We find also that kri-1/KRIT1 is required for host tolerance to bacterial infection, fecundity, and normal development. In this context, kri-1/KRIT1 restrains the activity of the cytoprotective transcription factor skn-1/NRF2 to control immune gene transcription and likely intestinal lipid mobilization during aging, a process necessary for healthy reproduction, but functions independently of skn-1/NRF2 to promote epithelial integrity and pathogen tolerance. These data reveal a broad role for a strongly conserved regulator in essential physiological processes that are required for reproductive fidelity and evolutionary success.

works.title: Conditional-prevalence correction for liability-scale analyses of covariate-adjusted binary GWAS
works.abstract: Adjustment for heritable covariates in genome-wide association studies of disease can induce collider bias, creating spurious genetic associations. Following bias correction, interpretation on the liability scale, which represents continuous disease susceptibility, requires an appropriate conversion from log odds. We derive this conversion under a Gaussian liability model for small genetic effects. The direct effect, excluding pathways through the adjusted covariates, and the collider-bias component share a common conversion factor. We characterize how this factor depends on variation in disease risk across covariate values and extend the derivation to case-control sampling. In simulations, the proposed conversion reduced the effect-size inflation associated with scaling based solely on disease prevalence. These results link existing collider-bias corrections to estimation of direct liability effects and clarify the interpretation of covariate-adjusted associations in population and case-control studies.

works.title: Repeatability of adaptation in interacting species
works.abstract: In many evolving systems, mutations have background-dependent fitness effects due to genetic interactions between loci within a genome (intragenomic epistasis). In coevolving species, genetic interactions can span across genomes, a phenomenon described as intergenomic epistasis. It is known that intragenomic epistasis can make adaptation more repeatable by constraining accessible mutational paths from a specific starting genotype, generating path repeatability. Here, we investigate how endpoint repeatability - how often adaptation from different starting genotypes reaches the same states in the genotype and fitness space - is influenced by the interplay of intra- and intergenomic epistasis. To this end, we model a two-species community in which the fitness of each genotype depends on the combination of present genotypes of both species. We implement this by constructing and simulating adaptation on coevolutionary fitness landscapes using an NKC(S) model, an extension of Kauffman's NK model of evolution that includes intergenomic epistasis. On these fitness landscapes, we simulate adaptive walks that alternate between mutations in a focal and a partner species. To quantify the repeatability of adaptation, we track the endpoints of adaptive walks and record the fitness of both species at the evolutionary endpoints. We find that individual fitness landscapes with intergenomic epistasis can maintain high endpoint repeatability. Yet, intergenomic epistasis causes highly variable fitness outcomes across different fitness landscapes. Thus, patterns of repeatability deviate from expectations based on single-species adaptation in the presence of intragenomic epistasis, due to varying fitness trade-offs between species, which can lead to cycling and large coevolutionary fitness loads.

works.title: Spatial single-cell mapping of transcriptional differences across genetic backgrounds in mouse brains
Foundation models unlock robust phenotypic representations from Cell Painting images

Multivalent ADAR1 recruitment for precise RNA editing
Similar small RNAs, different biological outcomes
Maternal age modulates progeny social behavior via a small RNA–neuropeptide axis
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Parental age influences offspring traits across species, yet the molecular pathways by which maternal state modulates progeny neural function remain poorly defined. Here we demonstrate that maternal age in C. elegans regulates progeny avoidance of the social pheromone by modulating the activity of a defined sensory circuit. Progeny of young mothers exhibit stronger activity of the pheromone-sensing ADL neurons and enhanced pheromone avoidance, whereas progeny of old mothers display reduced neuronal responses and weaker repulsion. We identify an ERI-1–microRNA–neuropeptide signaling axis operating in peptidergic AVH interneurons that modulates ADL circuit responsiveness. ERI-1 promotes expression of the neuropeptide gene flp-26 by repressing mir-8207 , and signaling from AVH to ADL establishes pheromone sensitivity. Maternal aging is associated with reduced ERI-1 expression in progeny AVH neurons and dampening this signaling pathway. Consequently, progeny of young mothers, though developmentally less robust, disperse more readily from crowded, pheromone-rich environments, offsetting their early-life disadvantages. Our findings reveal a molecular and circuit-level mechanism by which maternal physiology adaptively configures offspring neural computation and behavioral strategy across generations.

works.title: Distinct domains of Oligophrenin-1 regulate successive phases of cortical radial migration via RHOA- and PACSIN2-dependent mechanisms
works.abstract: Proper assembly of cortical circuits depends on the orderly migration of excitatory projection neurons, a multistep process marked by dynamic cell shape remodeling, including the transition from multipolar-to-bipolar morphology (MP-to-BP) followed by radial glial-guided locomotion. Although molecular players regulating individual stages have been identified, how these steps are coordinated remains unclear. Here, we uncover a critical role for the multidomain Rho-GAP oligophrenin-1 (OPHN1), an X-linked intellectual disability protein, as a dual-function regulator of radial migration. Using a molecular replacement strategy combined with live-cell imaging, we show that OPHN1 governs successive phases of migration through distinct domains and mechanisms: its GAP domain promotes the MP-to-BP transition by suppressing RHOA-ROCK signaling, whereas its second proline-rich domain regulates leading process remodeling and nucleokinesis during locomotion via interaction with the protein kinase C and casein kinase substrate in neurons 2 (PACSIN2). Together, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for OPHN1 in early cortical development and demonstrate that its domain-specific functions facilitate stepwise control of radial migration during corticogenesis.

works.title: Telomere-to-telomere genome of a dodecaploid desert shrub Prunus pedunculata reveals polyploidy-driven arid adaptation
works.abstract: Abstract Background Geographical imbalance in extremophile plant genomics has left the Mongolian Plateau underexplored. Prunus pedunculata , a desert shrub endemic to this arid region, provides an ideal system for understanding woody plant adaptation to extreme drought, yet its genomic architecture remains unknown. Results Here we present a telomere-to-telomere genome assembly for P. pedunculata , a dodecaploid (2n = 12 × = 96) with the highest ploidy level among sequenced woody perennials. Its 1.38 Gb genome is resolved into 48 chromosomes, and telomeric repeats are detected in each. Evolutionary analysis confirms an autopolyploid origin with > 80% subgenome consistency and no evidence of hybridization. The most recent whole-genome duplication dates to approximately 3.49 million years ago, coinciding with the uplift of the Tibetan Plateau and the intensification of Asian interior aridity. Ancestral karyotype reconstruction using six Prunus species spanning diploid to dodecaploid genomes and three inflorescence types reveals an eight chromosome ancestor and post polyploidization chromosomal rearrangements. Organ specific transcriptomics under progressive drought uncovers a coordinated division of labor that integrates ABA, CLE25 , BES1 / BIN2 , and auxin signaling modules to orchestrate growth cessation and stress survival. Drought induced genes significantly overlap with expanded gene families, demonstrating functional recruitment of polyploidy derived redundancy. Conclusions This work confirms an autopolyploid origin for P. pedunculata and links this polyploidization event to the aridification of the Asian interior. Duplicated genes have been repurposed for drought stress, and a multi-component signaling network coordinates organ responses and enhances survival under water scarcity, offering leads for crop improvement.

works.title: OpenAntigens: a structure-aware database for antigen construct design across the human cell-surface and secreted proteome
works.abstract: Choosing which region of a protein to express remains poorly standardized in antibody discovery, recombinant reagent generation, structural biology, and computational binder design. For human cell-surface and secreted proteins, this requires reconciling topology, processing, predicted, and experimental structure, modifications, interaction partners, orthologs, paralogs, and cross-reactivity risk before ordering DNA. OpenAntigens is a free, no-login database of construct-design reports for 5328 human secreted, GPI-anchored, single-pass, and multipass proteins. It integrates UniProt topology, AlphaFold pLDDT and PAE, PDB precedent, InterPro and Pfam domains, mouse and cynomolgus orthologs, paralog and family context, Open Targets disease associations, partner and assembly context, and BLAST searches. It provides 55 305 construct suggestions spanning full design regions, PDB-backed boundaries, annotated domains, pLDDT/PAE-derived regions, and membrane-expression options, plus 148 722 sequence-similarity hits to help choose constructs and assess cross-reactivity. For targets with compatible AlphaFold models, the interactive designer links sequence, structure, pLDDT, and PAE, allowing users to revise boundaries and export species-equivalent sequences with real-time cysteine and modification warnings. OpenAntigens places reproducible construct suggestions, comparative context, and browser editing in one workflow, reducing manual reconciliation across resources. OpenAntigens is available at openantigens.org.

works.title: BacMap 3.0: a comprehensive knowledgebase of annotated bacterial genomes
works.abstract: BacMap 3.0 (https://bacmap.ca) is a comprehensive, freely accessible resource integrating 23 524 bacterial and archaeal species, 32 866 genomes, >100 million genes, 1756 primary metabolic pathways, and 45 284 metabolites within one interactive platform. Despite the extraordinary growth of bacterial and archaeal genome sequencing, relevant data remain distributed across numerous specialized databases, impeding comprehensive genome-to-function analysis. While existing microbial resources generally emphasize genome annotation, taxonomy, metabolic pathways, or phenotypes separately, BacMap 3.0 unifies these complementary information layers within an organism-centred framework. It resolves this fragmentation by consolidating genomic, functional, structural, metabolic, phenotypic, ecological, and phylogenetic information into richly detailed, organism-specific "BacCards". Each BacCard combines an interactive genome map with extensive annotations covering bacterium-specific taxonomy, physiology, morphology, metabolism, protein structures, pathways, and metabolites. To facilitate data exploration, BacMap 3.0 supports taxonomic and phenotype-based browsing, chemical structure searches, interactive genome visualization, as well as gene, genome, 16S RNA, and protein BLAST searches. Building on earlier releases devoted primarily to genome visualization, BacMap 3.0 increases organismal coverage by >13-fold and transforms BacMap into an integrated bacterial knowledgebase for genome-to-function investigation across multiple biological scales. By bringing diverse biological information together in a single searchable environment, BacMap 3.0 offers a powerful platform for comparative genomics, microbiome research, infectious disease investigation, and biotechnology with a goal of accelerating the interpretation of microbial diversity, biology, and function.

works.title: MitImpact 4: a genome-wide resource for the interpretation of coding and non-coding mitochondrial DNA variants
works.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA variants are a frequent cause of inherited disease, yet their computational interpretation has focused almost exclusively on the 13 protein-coding genes. Variants in tRNA and rRNA genes, which carry a disproportionate share of the known pathogenic alleles, have remained a diagnostic blind spot, because their effect depends on RNA structure rather than on protein sequence and few dedicated predictors exist. MitImpact 4 removes this asymmetry. The database now covers all 49 704 single-nucleotide variants that can occur in the mitochondrial genome and reports their functional consequence, phylogenetic conservation, local mutational constraint, and population frequency in gnomAD, HelixMTdb, and ToMMo. Missense variants are annotated with APOGEE 2 and with newly added predictors, including AlphaMissense, ESM1b, VARITY, and LIST-S2, while tRNA and rRNA variants receive predictions from nAPOGEE, our RNA-specific model, alongside MitoTIP and PON-mt-tRNA. For both classes, scores are accompanied by posterior probabilities of pathogenicity that can be used within the ACMG/AMP framework for mitochondrial DNA. Clinical annotation from ClinVar and MITOMAP, including ClinGen expert-panel classifications, is integrated in a redesigned interface that also annotates user-submitted VCF files. MitImpact 4 is freely available at https://mitimpact.mcb2lab.org.

works.title: scMRdb: a comprehensive resource for cell-type-resolved Mendelian randomization of complex traits
works.abstract: Mendelian randomization (MR) is a powerful analytical approach to infer putative causal links between gene expression and human disease, using genetic variants as instrumental variables to mitigate confounding and reverse causation. However, existing MR resources predominantly rely on bulk-tissue expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs), which mask cell-type-specific transcriptional effects by averaging expression across cellular populations. Furthermore, cell-type-resolved causal evidence from single-cell eQTL (sc-eQTL) MR analyses remains fragmented across individual studies with inconsistent workflows, prohibiting standardized cross-cell-type comparisons. Here we present scMRdb (https://ngdc.cncb.ac.cn/scmrdb), a comprehensive resource for cell-type-resolved MR of human complex traits and diseases. scMRdb harmonizes 5206 genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics of European and East Asian ancestry with 585 sc-eQTL datasets spanning 11 tissues and cell systems, including 110 cell types. A uniform pipeline evaluates all gene-trait pairs via MR followed by Steiger directionality testing. Significant associations are assessed by colocalization, and results are stratified into six confidence tiers with integrated drug-target annotation. scMRdb enables systematic recovery of candidate causal genes supported by cell-type-resolved regulatory evidence that is often diluted or obscured in bulk-tissue analyses. We expect scMRdb to serve as a user-friendly portal for generating cell-type-informed mechanistic hypotheses and prioritizing actionable therapeutic targets for complex human diseases.

works.title: MetabHub: an integrative platform for plasma nuclear magnetic resonance metabolomics using mediation analysis, disease prediction, and risk stratification
works.abstract: Plasma nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) metabolomics offers a scalable molecular readout linking genetic variation, environmental exposure, and clinical physiology to future disease risk. Existing resources typically address metabolite-disease associations, metabolite quantitative trait loci, or prediction separately, with limited support for integrated mediation and longitudinal risk stratification. MetabHub (https://www.metabhub.net) is a web-based resource built from individual-level UK Biobank data, comprising 364 795 European participants, 251 plasma NMR traits, 129 clinical measurements, 54 environmental exposures, genome-wide variants, and 57 incident diseases. It maps sex-combined and sex-specific associations across measurements, exposures, genotypes, metabolites, and diseases, yielding 2 950 764 significant associations. Using two-step screening and natural effect models, MetabHub identifies 1 886 224 significant clinical measurement, environmental factor, and genotype mediation pathways. It also provides metabolite-based prediction models for incident disease using penalized logistic regression, XGBoost, LightGBM, and multilayer perceptron, together with an online interface for applying pre-trained models to user-uploaded profiles. Model-derived metabolomic risk scores are further evaluated using Cox regression and survival stratification over ~14 years of follow-up. Global search, interactive visualization, downloadable tables, prediction, and stratification modules support mechanistic discovery and metabolomics-informed precision prevention.

works.title: The lipid raft marker flotillin FloA drives relocalization of the plasma membrane H+-ATPase PmaA as a protective response to calcium stress
works.abstract: Biological membranes are laterally heterogeneous and contain specialized microdomains called lipid rafts. Lipid rafts serve as organizational platforms that cluster signaling molecules or modulate membrane protein conformation through their unique lipid environment. There are specific lipid raft marker proteins whose functions remain obscure. One of these proteins is flotillin which has been linked to endocytosis. Here, we investigated the regulation and function of FloA, the sole flotillin homolog in the model fungus Aspergillus nidulans . FloA expression is specifically upregulated in response to calcium stress, which is a regulatory pattern also conserved in Aspergillus fumigatus . BioID proximity labeling revealed that A. nidulans FloA physically interacts with proteins in the endocytic pathway as well as another lipid raft marker, the plasma membrane H + -ATPase PmaA. Under calcium stress, PmaA undergoes internalization from the cytoplasmic membrane. However, when floA is deleted, PmaA internalization is prevented, resulting in cell death. This phenotype of the Δ floA strain could be mimicked by treating the cells with an endocytosis inhibitor during calcium stress. Together, we demonstrate that FloA is essential for the internalization of PmaA during calcium stress, a process that prevents intracellular calcium overload and promotes cell viability. Our results also provide further evidence for flotillin-assisted endocytosis.

works.title: Nicotinic receptor in dopamine neurons mediates learned odor choice
works.abstract: Nicotinic acetylcholine signaling modulates dopaminergic output in mammalian midbrain circuits and can thereby influence decision-making. In Drosophila, dopamine neurons (DANs) in the protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) cluster convey sugar reward signals and promote approach toward a rewarded odor after associative learning. Although nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) have been implicated in regulating PAM DAN excitability and transmitter release, how this modulation supports specific cognitive operations during learning and memory remains unclear. Here, we tested the role of nAChRs in PAM DANs in odor-sugar associative learning and memory. Among nine nAChR genes examined, loss of the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor α1 subunit (Dα1) in PAM neurons impaired appetitive memory. Consistent with this requirement, Dα1 was detected in these DANs at both the transcript and protein levels, with Dα1 puncta observed in PAM axon-terminal and putative dendritic regions. Importantly, live imaging showed that Dα1 knockdown in PAM DANs attenuated odor-evoked synaptic Ca2+ signals, whereas sugar-evoked Ca2+ responses were largely preserved. Behaviorally, Dα1 knockdown in PAM DANs reduced performance in a two-odor forced-choice discrimination task, whereas no performance deficit was detected across the single-odor pursuit conditions or innate odor choice. Together, these results identify a nicotinic mechanism in PAM DANs that supports odor-evoked synaptic activity and contributes to learned odor-choice performance when competing odor cues are present.

works.title: Genome compartmentalization in a fungal insect pathogen reveals a second mating-type locus on an accessory chromosome
works.abstract: The genomes of many fungal pathogens include rapidly evolving regions with high transposable element densities. Such regions often contain genes important for pathogenicity and may be non-core genomic elements carried on accessory chromosomes that are variably present among isolates considered to be members of the same species. Here we present a pangenomic analysis of a fungal insect pathogen, Metarhizium acridum, using six chromosomal assemblies that include isolates from four different continents. We show that the pangenome of M. acridum exhibits a continuum of compartmentalization, with a core genome that contains most of the carbohydrate-active enzymes, while accessory genes are primarily located in gene-sparse regions which encode many small secreted proteins, termed effectors, that are active during host interaction. Furthermore, we identified the first accessory chromosome in M. acridum. In contrast to the accessory chromosomes of many other fungal species, this chromosome does not encode any known effectors or secondary metabolite proteins related to pathogen-host interactions. Instead, the accessory chromosome is enriched in functions related to sexual reproduction and carries genes from both the MAT1-1 and MAT1-2 mating-type idiomorphs, in addition to the canonical MAT locus found on the core chromosomes. Notable as, within the genus Metarhizium, M. acridum is one of few species considered to regularly reproduce sexually. Our findings suggest that the presence of this accessory chromosome further facilitates sexual reproduction, possibly even primary homothallism, in the otherwise heterothallic M. acridum. Overall, our study suggests a novel mechanism in which an accessory chromosome may enhance the capacity for a fungal pathogen to undergo recombination.

works.title: Inferring the multi-host fitness landscape of endive necrotic mosaic virus from cross-inoculation experiments
works.abstract: Fitness landscapes offer a compact representation of adaptation, yet are rarely inferred from sparse multi-environment data. We present a Bayesian approach to infer an effective multi-host phenotypic fitness landscape from cross-inoculation assays by linking successful infection probabilities to Fisher's geometrical model and to an explicit decomposition of establishment routes. The model estimates (i) the distance matrix among host-specific phenotypic optima, (ii) target-host permissiveness through the widths of fitness peaks, (iii) target-specific differences in the efficiency with which phenotypic suitability translates into successful infection, and (iv) the conditional probabilities that successful infections are attributed to direct establishment, rescue from standing variation in the source inoculum, or de novo rescue in the target host. We apply the approach to an experimental evolution dataset for endive necrotic mosaic virus evolved on five Asteraceae hosts and challenged in a full cross-inoculation design. The inferred landscape can be visualized as a phenotypic map of the host community, revealing pronounced heterogeneity in target-host permissiveness and a geometry broadly concordant with host phylogeny. By grounding assay-derived distances in an explicit mechanistic model, the approach provides a parsimonious representation of multi-host constraints that can be used to discuss establishment barriers and potential springboard hosts in heterogeneous communities. More broadly, it offers a general method for inferring effective fitness landscapes from sparse multi-environment data.

works.title: Genetic architecture of cichlid brain morphology
works.abstract: How evolutionary and developmental processes interact to determine axes of neural variation that produce behavioural diversity has been debated for many decades, with alternative hypotheses giving differential emphasis to functional coupling, which favours co-evolution, and developmental constraint, which enforces it. A critical omission is data on the genetic architecture of brain size and structure, which more closely illuminates the shared developmental dependencies between components of an integrated system. Here, we exploit ecological divergence between Astatotilapia calliptera and Aulonocara stuartgranti, two closely related cichlid species from Lake Malawi, to explore the genetic architecture of brain evolution. Using computer vision and machine learning techniques to extract volumetric data from micro-tomographic images, we first demonstrate significant divergence in brain composition between these species. Genomic and micro-tomographic imaging data from a population of hybrids generated between the two species were used to investigate genetic factors shaping this differentiation. We show that the majority of brain components are integrated phenotypically in hybrids, but genetic correlations between them are generally weaker. We further show that variation in multiple brain components is associated with variation in largely structure-specific quantitative trait loci, rather than determined by genetic factors with broad effects across the entire brain. These results suggest a genetic architecture that can facilitate modular changes in brain structure, and imply that individual components are independently evolvable.

works.title: Yra2 regulates proteolysis of Cse4 to prevent its mislocalization to non-centromeric regions for chromosomal stability in budding yeast
works.abstract: Abstract Restricting the centromere-specific histone H3 variant Cse4 (CENP-A in human) to centromeric chromatin ensures faithful chromosome segregation. Mislocalization of overexpressed Cse4/CENP-A to non-centromeric regions contributes to chromosomal instability (CIN), an important hallmark of many cancers. Hence, defining mechanisms that prevent mislocalization of Cse4 is clinically significant. Here we report a role for YRA2 (Yeast RNA Annealing Protein 2) in ubiquitin mediated proteolysis of Cse4 to prevent its mislocalization for chromosomal stability. YRA2 was identified in a genome-wide screen for gene deletions that exhibit synthetic dosage lethality (SDL) upon overexpression of CSE4 (GALCSE4). We determined that yra2Δ strains exhibit increased Cse4 stability, enriched Cse4 chromatin association, reduced Cse4 ubiquitination, Cse4 mislocalization, and CIN. Defects in interaction of E3 ubiquitin ligase Psh1 with Cse4 contributes to stability of Cse4 in yra2Δ strains. Consistent with these results, overexpression of PSH1 suppresses GALCSE4 SDL in yra2Δ strain. Yra2 mediated proteolysis of Cse4 is separable from its RNA related functions as GALCSE4 SDL was not observed in yra2F96A,F108A strain with mutations in Yra2 RNA recognition motif. Furthermore, poly(A)+ RNA export mutants in YRA1 (yra1-2) and MEX67 (mex67-5), that interact with Yra2, do not exhibit GALCSE4 SDL and defects in RNA export are not observed in yra2Δ cells. We determined that evolutionarily conserved C-terminal ChTOP domain of Yra2 with an intact N-terminal RNA binding domain exhibits GALCSE4 SDL and defects in Cse4 proteolysis. In summary, we have defined a role for Yra2 in preventing mislocalization of Cse4 by facilitating its proteolysis for chromosomal stability.

works.title: A candidate genetic trigger of female sex determination in Marsabit clawed frogs ( Xenopus borealis )
works.abstract: A central question in biology asks why the genetic basis of sex determination evolves quickly in some groups even though disruption of this process carries severe risks such as sterility. A challenge to understanding mechanisms of this rapid evolution is a lack of functionally verified genetic triggers of sex determination. To begin to remedy this, we set out to identify, characterize, and functionally test the genetic trigger of female sex determination in Marsabit clawed frogs (Xenopus borealis), which has a species-specific and probably newly evolved W chromosome. Genomic and transcriptomic data identify a candidate that was expressed specifically in female gonads during sex determination. We knocked out this gene, which is a female-specific duplicate of wnt3.L - hereafter wnt3-W - and induced complete female-to-male sex reversal in 35 of 36 individuals. These sex-reversed individuals had male-typical external and internal morphology, mating behavior, mating calls, testis histology, and are fertile. This demonstrates that wnt3-W is generally necessary for feminization of X. borealis, and adds to only one other functionally verified candidate trigger of sex determination in amphibians. Phylogenetic and cytogenetic analysis indicates that wnt3-W originated recently on the tip of the X. borealis W chromosome, after this species diverged from all other extant Xenopus. Wnt3-W is the first known candidate genetic trigger of sex determination in the Wnt gene family, which is surprising because wnt3 is more generally involved with vital, but not sex-specific functions. Similarities in protein structure are consistent with the possibility that Wnt3-W is a genetic surrogate that utilizes the feminizing genetic network of Wnt4. The discovery of wnt3-W adds to a handful of other secreted peptides that trigger sex determination in animals; its proposed function as a positively acting female-determining gene - if confirmed - would further be distinguished from other known genetic triggers in vertebrates.

works.title: m⁶A presence and dosage are associated with IGF2BP2 binding, RNA abundance, and translation in mouse heart and liver
works.abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m⁶A), the most prevalent internal modification in mammalian mRNA, contributes to post-transcriptional gene regulation, yet how m⁶A presence and modification intensity relate to gene expression during development remains incompletely understood. Here, by integrating m⁶A-seq, RNA-seq, IGF2BP2 RIP-seq, and Ribo-seq data across developmental trajectories of murine heart and liver, we identify a genome-wide presence-dosage pattern of m⁶A-associated gene regulation. m⁶A-modified transcripts generally show higher baseline expression than unmodified transcripts, whereas increasing modification intensity within m⁶A-modified transcripts is associated with reduced transcript abundance. This dual pattern is linked to the binding behavior of the m⁶A reader IGF2BP2: IGF2BP2 occupancy is enriched on m⁶A-modified transcripts but decreases with higher methylation intensity. Structural equation modeling further supports layered associations among m⁶A status, IGF2BP2 binding, transcript abundance, and ribosome occupancy. Regional analysis of m⁶A peaks also suggests position-dependent relationships with translation efficiency, with 3' UTR m⁶A associated with higher TE and CDS m⁶A associated with lower TE. Together, our study provides a quantitative multi-omic framework for understanding how m⁶A presence and dosage are associated with gene expression and translation during tissue development, and suggests IGF2BP2 binding as a potential mediator of these relationships.

works.title: Cytoplasmic mRNA recapping is essential for stress recovery and intracellular proliferation in Trypanosoma cruzi
works.abstract: , the causative agent of Chagas disease, regulates gene expression predominantly after transcription because it lacks conventional gene-specific promoters. Cytoplasmic mRNA recapping has been proposed to restore translation-competent mRNAs from silenced transcripts, but its physiological role in kinetoplastids has remained unclear. Here, we show that the cytoplasmic capping enzyme TcCe1 supports transcriptome homeostasis, an effective heat-shock response, and productive intracellular infection of host cells. TcCe1 loss was associated with reduced transcript abundance across extended polycistronic transcription units, impaired induction of proteostasis factors under stress, altered steady-state abundance of uncapped transcripts detected by ligation-mediated RT-qPCR, and marked defects in recovery and infectivity. Because cytoplasmic recapping in kinetoplastids is mechanistically distinct from host pathways, TcCe1 may represent a promising target for parasite-selective therapeutics. Together, our findings highlight the importance of TcCe1 in RNA-level regulation, environmental responsiveness, and host adaptation in this early-branching eukaryote.

works.title: Antisense Oligonucleotides with 5′-decoy technology triggers nonsense-mediated decay of SCN9A to elicit long-lasting analgesia
works.abstract: The voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.7 (SCN9A) is a genetically validated target for pain therapy, but achieving therapeutic isoform selectivity remains a formidable challenge for small-molecule inhibitors. Here, we overcome this bottleneck through a highly selective RNA-targeted strategy that dictates SCN9A alternative splicing. We first identified ASO50 as the most potent baseline candidate antisense oligonucleotide (ASO). Subsequent 5'-decoy (5D) sequence screening yielded an upgraded candidate, L9C-ASO50, which is engineered to competitively intercept U1 snRNA, achieving a cooperative spatial hindrance that robustly suppresses exon 5 recognition. This targeted exon exclusion introduces a frameshift that triggers robust, obligate transcript clearance via the nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) pathway, ensuring complete functional silencing without cross-reacting with homologous NaV channels. Mechanistically, we define the underlying cis-trans regulatory architecture, revealing a homeostatic tug-of-war where the RNA-binding protein ELAVL2 enforces exon inclusion, paradoxically antagonized by the canonical SR protein family. Crucially, CNS-restricted delivery of L9C-ASO50 produces profound and sustained mechanical and thermal analgesia. These findings establish splice-modulated transcript degradation as a viable therapeutic paradigm for chronic pain and provide a broadly applicable blueprint for engineering targeted RNA therapeutics.

works.title: ESMRank: learning-to-rank prediction of missense variant effects from deep mutational scanning data
works.abstract: Abstract Predicting the functional effects of missense variants is limited both by predictor performance and by the lack of principled strategies to integrate heterogeneous multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs), including deep mutational scanning, into transferable sequence-function models. Here, we show that redundancy among partially overlapping deep mutational scanning experiments, often treated as noise, yields a consensus landscape of mutational constraint. We introduce “variant soundness”, an overlap-aware rank-fusion score that uses cross-experiment consistency to derive an assay-agnostic ordering of mutational tolerance within proteins. Applied to ~1100 MAVEs spanning over two million missense variants, this approach reveals a mutational landscape enriched for structural stability constraints. Guided by this integrated signal, we develop ESMRank, a sequence-based learning-to-rank predictor combining ESM2 representations with physicochemical descriptors. Under strict protein-level partitioning, ESMRank outperforms widely used predictors across abundance-, folding-, and stability-related assays in ProteinGym and Domainome. Predicted deleterious variants are enriched for ClinVar pathogenicity and, in CFTR, correlate with folding efficiency, channel activity, and pharmacological responsiveness. Together, these results turn assay redundancy into a scalable resource for interpretable missense variant prediction.

works.title: Population-scale ancestral recombination graphs with tskit 1.0
Advancing morphological profiling with self-supervised learning through comparative insights into representation learning of cellular perturbations
works.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) enables scalable, label-free foundation models (FMs) that learn task-agnostic representations directly from images, bypassing cell segmentation and feature engineering inherent to classical morphological profiling. We present a large-scale evaluation of SSL FMs for image-based phenotypic profiling, covering contrastive (DINO), masked-based generative (MAE, iTPN) and hybrid (DINOv2) learning mechanisms, pretrained on all unannotated chemical perturbations from the Joint Undertaking for Morphological Profiling-Cell Painting (JUMP-CP) dataset (119,876 compounds, ~1.77 million images, 7 laboratories). Here we show that top-performing SSL models outperformed CellProfiler in compound-replicate retrieval on the held-out JUMP-Target2 set (302 annotated compounds, P ≤ 0.001). DINO and DINOv2 generalized across diverse perturbations and cell types, outperforming CellProfiler with 31-37% gains in site-averaged mean average precision for mechanism-of-action retrieval on EU-OPENSCREEN Bioactives (2,464 compounds), and consistently surpassing masked-based models across all benchmarks. This study provides a systematic assessment of SSL approaches for advancing morphological profiling and offers pretrained FMs to accelerate drug discovery.

works.title: Enhanced cfDNA methylation profiling by detection and correction of jagged ends
works.abstract: Analysis of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation can enable noninvasive disease detection by leveraging tissue-specific epigenetic differences between malignant and nonmalignant cells. However, such analyses can be confounded by the repair of jagged DNA fragment ends during double-stranded sequencing library preparation, which introduces spurious methylation signals into cfDNA molecules. Here we present JEEPERS, a framework to detect and correct jagged-end-induced methylation errors while preserving duplex integrity and native methylation patterns. We showed high fidelity for measuring tumor burden and demonstrated allele-specific methylation differences at recurrent somatic mutations, revealing a link between adjacent CpG methylation and EGFR/TP53 driver and resistance mutations. We further demonstrated enhanced diagnostic performance across liquid biopsy applications, including tumor-type-specific methylation profiles, hemimethylation profiling, epigenetic-clock-based age estimation and cell type deconvolution. By faithfully correcting end-repair errors, JEEPERS provides a versatile framework for integrating mutations and methylation features in cfDNA at high resolution, enabling more precise molecular profiling and disease monitoring.

works.title: Population-scale single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of skeletal muscle reveals extensive context-specific genetic regulation
Tracing cell fate in space and time with SPACE-seq
Chemogenomic profiling of diverse Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains using the novel CRISPR-Cas9 markerless barcoded library BarMix
works.abstract: Natural populations are rich reservoirs of genetic variation, and incorporating this diversity into functional genomic screens can reveal the genetic and phylogenetic determinants underlying trait differences. Genetic barcoding is a powerful tool for yeast functional genomics, enabling scalable fitness profiling and high-throughput gene-trait interaction mapping. Nevertheless, few barcoded libraries capture the natural diversity of Saccharomyces cerevisiae . Here, we introduce BarMix, a novel barcoded library of diverse S. cerevisiae strains designed and validated for high-throughput fitness profiling. Using CRISPR-Cas9, we integrate distinct markerless genetic barcodes into the genomes of 262 strains representing multiple phylogenetic clades of wild, domesticated, and admixed origins. To evaluate its utility for genotype–phenotype mapping, we quantitatively profile the pooled library by barcode-sequencing against 33 small-molecule compounds with diverse bioactivities and identify 281 chemogenomic interactions through genome-wide association analysis. Chemical fitness signatures differ between domesticated and wild clades, particularly under stresses affecting ergosterol biosynthesis, DNA alkylation, microtubule depolymerisation, TORC1 inactivation, and membrane permeability. We validate seven associated alleles through allele-swap experiments, including variants in genes that modulate multidrug export (Yrr1), tRNA-specificity (ArgRS), and small-molecule methylation (Crg1). Several alleles display variable penetrance across strains, suggesting a complex genetic basis for trait variation. Importantly, including admixture into the genome-wide association design enhances variant detection in S. cerevisiae . These results establish BarMix as a powerful platform for genotype–phenotype discovery with diverse applications in functional genomics and biotechnology, and highlight the value of incorporating natural variation into model-systems biology.

works.title: Cis-regulatory co-option of a transposon family reinforces cell identity across the immune system
works.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) comprise about half of the human and mouse genomes and contribute to gene regulation during immune responses. However, how TEs acquire cis-regulatory functions during immune cell development remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed hundreds of datasets profiling chromatin accessibility, gene expression, transcription factor occupancy and DNA-DNA contact across diverse mouse and human immune cell types. We identified two rodent-specific TE subfamilies, ORR1E and ORR1D2 (collectively, ODE) that have diversified after genomic insertion into cell type-specific enhancers across the mouse immune system. Post-insertion mutations in ODE loci generated differential binding sites for lineage-specifying transcription factors. ODEs showed evidence of evolutionary sequence constraint and contacted promoters of hundreds of genes in immune cells. Predicted ODE target genes were enriched for cell type-specific functions and showed increased expression in mouse compared to human cell types lacking ODEs. Together, these findings show how a single TE family can diversify after genomic spread to generate cell type-specific enhancers that reinforce lineage-specific gene programs.

works.title: Modeling long-range human nigrostriatal connectivity in vitro reveals striatal target-dependent maturation of dopamine neurons
works.abstract: The human nigrostriatal pathway, comprising dopaminergic neurons in the ventral midbrain that project to the dorsolateral striatum, is essential for motor control and selectively vulnerable in Parkinson's disease. How this circuit assembles during human development remains poorly understood, and in vitro models capturing its long-range connectivity and spatial organization have been lacking. Here, we establish a compartmentalized, human stem cell-based model of the nigrostriatal pathway by integrating ventral midbrain and striatal organoids within a custom-engineered microfluidic device that confines cell bodies while guiding axonal growth to recapitulate key aspects of in vivo topography. Functional connectivity was confirmed by retrograde rabies tracing, and optogenetic and pharmacological stimulation. Single-nucleus transcriptomic analysis reveals that axonal target engagement with spatially separated striatal neurons promotes maturation of human dopaminergic neurons and activates transcriptional programs associated with neurotransmitter secretion. Our study establishes a biologically relevant in vitro system for investigating how long-range connectivity regulates neuronal assembly in the nigrostriatal circuit and for modelling key pathological features of Parkinson's disease.

works.title: Fast probabilistic whitening transformation for ultra-high dimensional genetic data
works.abstract: Statistical methods often make assumptions about independence between the samples or features of a dataset, yet correlation structure is ubiquitous in real data. In statistical genetics, correlation between regression summary statistics due to linkage disequilibrium (LD) between nearby variants complicates downstream analysis. Many methods use LD reference panels to account for this correlation. Whitening transformations comprise a family of methods to remove correlation structure, and are used implicitly by many common models. Here we propose a probabilistic model for data whitening, and propose parameter estimates and efficient algorithms to improve statistical and computational performance. In an application to impute z-statistics from unobserved genetic variants from a genome-wide association study of schizophrenia, the probabilistic whitening transformation, had the lowest mean square error while being up to an order of magnitude faster than other methods. Using this approach, we also identify tandem repeats that explain genetic regulatory signals for disease-relevant genes. Analyses are implemented in our novel open source R packages decorrelate and imputez .

works.title: Synthetic collinearization of a chromosome segment enables genetic dissection of incompatibility between distant genera
works.abstract: Reproductive barriers and genomic structural differences hinder genetic analysis between highly divergent organisms. Here, we examined whether these challenges can be overcome by collinearization, the synthesis of chromosomes that retain the native gene content and organization of a host organism while incorporating the DNA sequences of another organism. We applied collinearization to Kluyveromyces marxianus, a yeast species that is both distantly related to and has a distinct genome structure from the model yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. We generated a ∼35-kb K. marxianus DNA segment that was collinear with one-sixth of a S. cerevisiae chromosome and contained 17 protein-coding genes. Although this synthetic chromosome segment successfully substituted for its native counterpart in an S. cerevisiae cell, it imposed a significant growth cost due to the incompatibility of two K. marxianus proteins with the host proteome. We attempted to predict disrupted protein-protein interactions using AlphaFold and fully or partially alleviated the resulting fitness costs by supplementing orthologous protein partners from K. marxianus. Furthermore, we completely eliminated the growth cost by replacing the incompatible K. marxianus genes with their S. cerevisiae orthologs. These findings demonstrate that collinearization can facilitate the creation of chimeric genomes to dissect the genetic basis of incompatibility and traits between organisms that cannot naturally hybridize. They also suggest that many genetic incompatibilities likely exist between S. cerevisiae and K. marxianus, reflecting disrupted protein-protein interactions that may to some degree be predictable in silico.

works.title: OBITUARY: Fritz Eckstein (1932–2026), a legend who shaped the Oligonucleotide Therapeutics field forever by giving it its backbone
Longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing of a neuroendocrine transdifferentiation model reveals transcriptional reprogramming in treatment-induced neuroendocrine prostate cancer
